intro: Class identifiers are names, but an ordinary numeric feature can make class two appear twice as large as class one.
task: Convert class labels to one-hot rows with a fixed, explicitly supplied number of classes.
requirements: labels is a nonempty finite vector of integer values from zero through num_classes - 1.
num_classes is a positive integer, excluding booleans. Unobserved classes still get columns.
Return a NumPy array with one at each label column and zero elsewhere.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

examples.name: Repeated classes
examples.output:
[[0, 0, 1], [1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1]]
(Numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places where needed.)

examples.name: Missing batch classes
examples.output:
[[0, 1, 0, 0]]
(Numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places where needed.)

examples.name: Single-class vocabulary
examples.output:
[[1.0], [1.0]]
(Numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places where needed.)

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Allocate zeros with shape (number of labels, num_classes), then index by row and label.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Validate integrality before casting; silently truncating 1.7 would change the category.

explanation: One-hot encoding preserves category identity without assigning a distance along a single number line. Each observation selects exactly one coordinate.
The number of columns comes from the declared vocabulary, not the largest label in this batch. A missing class must not change the representation used by the model.
Try two batches that contain different subsets of labels. Explain why inferring the output width independently would break a shared classifier.
